notes: The format assertion (json-passes-checker) favours the skill by construction — the baseline had no way to know the format. Without it: with_skill 21/21, baseline 17/21 (81%).

Discriminating content assertions: verbatim quotes on every item (baseline fails 2/3 — inferred items without quotes, line numbers only), 'between 1 and 3' assumed inclusive by baseline, and unlisted pairs treated as illegal by baseline where the spec has no blanket rule.

Baselines were strong on substance: all three found the main gaps (end ≤ start status, fine conflict, missing EXPIRED state) and marked their own inferences — the skill's edge is consistency and machine-checkable traceability, not insight.
Skill weakness 1 — BV step rule: 'step = unit the boundary is written in' gave a 1 h / 2 h / 3 h triple for the 2-hour cancel deadline (baseline: 119/120/121 min).

Skill weakness 2 — 'always three values' forces meaningless triples: duration BV-03 (−1/0/+1 min for strictly-after; +1 is invalid only because of the 15-min minimum) and library BV-04 age 11/12/13 all 'valid' (age selects a limit, it isn't valid/invalid).

Skill weakness 3 — SKILL.md lists 'up to' as a cue that settles inclusivity; the with_skill run therefore treated '2 hours before' as inclusive, while the baseline flagged it as ambiguous. The skill hard-codes an interpretation.
Cost: with_skill ~69k tokens / 190 s mean vs baseline ~50k / 100 s — the skill is ~40% more tokens and ~2× slower (exhaustive matrix, quote lookup, checker round).
